claim: ELI5: cycle 15 was not wrong, it was never run. HYP-0015 was pre-registered, challenged (advisory PROCEED) and then no candidate file and no score were ever produced, exactly the way cycle 12 vanished before cycle 13 re-ran it. So this cycle re-registers that design in full, standalone, and adds the one thing that changed underneath it: at 04:09Z the Director re-pinned the contract to run the five instances in parallel and to REQUIRE that a candidate use a fixed iteration budget and seed every RNG on payload['name'], never on wall-clock time or call order. HYP-0015's budget was a 420-second wall-clock deadline, which that rule now forbids, so the deadline is replaced by a deterministic fit-count budget and every seed is keyed to the instance name. Everything else is the cycle-15 diagnosis, restated. The grader adds two things: how many expensive two-qubit gates the circuit spends, plus a 1000x-weighted penalty for any fidelity shortfall below the published anchor for that instance. Cycle 14 removed about 13 gates spread over four of the five instances yet the mean only fell 2.60, because roughly 22 of the remaining points are not cost at all: they are about 0.022 of fidelity debt sitting on ONE instance. The arithmetic checks out against the two scored runs: cycle 13 emitted the full 35-gate circuit everywhere and scored 39.5234 per instance, so its total debt was (39.5234-35)*5/1000 = 0.0226 of fidelity; cycle 14's 184.61 total is 35 gates plus about 22.6 penalty points on one instance plus about 127 gates over the other four. The reason that instance is stuck is a line of code: workspace/incumbent.py:479-485 ABORTS the whole pruning loop whenever the full-35-gate fit lands more than 0.001 below that instance's anchor, so the one instance carrying the penalty is the one instance never allowed to delete a single gate. It keeps the debt AND all 35 gates, the worst of both. That abort was correct under the OLD fidelity-only metric. Under the current metric it is an arithmetic mistake: one gate is worth 1 point and 0.001 of fidelity is worth 1 point, so a removal that costs less than 0.001 of fidelity is a net gain EVEN on an instance already in debt. This cycle therefore deletes every threshold, margin and abort in the selection logic and replaces them with direct minimization of the grader's own published formula, which the candidate may compute because the five anchor fidelities are printed in CONTRACT.md's public Metric paragraph (0.8955, 0.9164, 0.9011, 0.9228, 0.9229) and are contract data, not battery data. Formally: keep the EXP-0014 target construction (H_tot dense from payload['h_cost'] with leftmost Pauli label character = qubit 0, T = normalize(expm(-beta*H_tot/4) @ payload['reference_state'])), the 8-Hadamard prefix that costs 0 on the two-qubit axis, the masked hardware-efficient block (6 layers of rz/rx on 8 qubits interleaved with 5 linear chains cx(q,q+1), q=0..6, slot s = 7*layer+q), the adjoint-gradient L-BFGS-B fit primitive, the import-time topology and gradient gates, all byte-identical; change only (a) the decision rule, to s_hat = 1000*max(0, anchor + 0.0005 - F_self) + C2 driving accept, reject and emit, with every evaluated (mask, theta) point recorded in a trace and the ARG-MIN of that trace emitted, so the run can never emit a point worse than the best point it has seen; (b) the abort, deleted, replaced by a pre-registered escalated multistart on any instance whose full-mask fit lands below its anchor (the sealed anchor for Row 30 itself needed the Director's 12-init escalation to be found, JOURNAL 2026-09-21 23:20Z, so a deficit is a basin miss, not evidence of a structural limit); and (c) the budget, from wall-clock seconds to a fixed count of trial fits with name-keyed seeds, as the re-pinned contract now requires.
prediction: Mean score falls from the incumbent's 36.9214 to <= 34.9 (Delta <= -2.0) with valid=true on all five instances. Mechanism-specific predictions, all recorded in DIAG before the score is known: (1) exactly one instance has F_full below its anchor by 0.015 to 0.030 on the full 35-slot mask, i.e. the abort path in the incumbent would have fired there and nowhere else, confirming the debt is single-instance; (2) that instance's own s_hat falls from about 57.6 to <= 40, contributing >= 3.5 of the mean improvement, through some combination of >= 3 accepted removals (now that the abort is gone) and a partial or full close of the 0.022 debt by the escalated multistart; (3) the four already-pruned instances do not regress, because the greedy descent under the same fixed budget reaches their cycle-14 endpoints and the trace arg-min protects them; (4) the run is deterministic: no decision reads wall-clock time, so a rerun on the same host reproduces the same emitted circuits gate-for-gate. If the escalated multistart closes the debt fully on the deficit instance the mean lands <= 33.0 and the contract's ship condition is met; that is the upside case, NOT the prediction I am betting on.
falsifier: The scorer returns a score >= 36.8214, i.e. an improvement smaller than the contract's min_improvement of 0.1. Because the emitted point is the arg-min of s_hat over a trace that always contains the full-mask best-angle point, and because each pruned instance's cycle-14 endpoint is reachable inside the same greedy descent under the same fixed fit budget, a non-improvement falsifies the DIAGNOSIS rather than the implementation: it would mean the roughly 1.9-points-per-instance gap between 36.92 and the 35-gate cost floor, plus the four instances' remaining cost, is not a single-instance fidelity debt created by the abort path. The DIAG fields that decide which reading is right are all recorded pre-score: per instance final_cost, final_F_self, anchor, s_hat_emitted, stop_reason, the full s_hat trace, the escalation records, and fits_used. A second, separately recorded falsification: if on the deficit instance the escalation reaches F_full >= anchor + 0.0005 but the descent then accepts zero removals, the debt was real and closable while the structure is incompressible at that instance, which is a different finding from a wrong score decomposition and must be logged as such rather than folded into the headline.
kill_threshold: Kill this direction (selection-rule and optimizer-budget refinement of the hardware-efficient block) if EITHER (a) the scorer returns a score > 36.9214, i.e. strictly worse than the incumbent, or (b) the score improves by < 0.1 AND DIAG shows no instance with a fidelity debt above 0.002 on its emitted point, which would mean the score decomposition above is wrong and the remaining points are cost that greedy backward elimination with refit simply cannot reach. On either kill, block pruning closes at the measured crossing cost, the campaign records that cost as the certified compressibility limit of the layered rz/rx-plus-linear-chain family, and cycle 17 must move to the other mechanism family named in the contract: heavily term-pruned ma-QAOA layers built from payload['h_cost'] (analytic price 6 CNOTs per weight-4 string, so about 5 surviving four-body terms plus the 1-CX |I> prep to land under 35), pitched as a macro structural bet.
brief:
CODER BRIEF. Edit ONLY workspace/candidate.py. Start by copying workspace/incumbent.py (the EXP-0014 candidate) VERBATIM, then make exactly the changes in B1-B9 and nothing else.

DO NOT TOUCH (audit-confirmed, stays byte-identical): the baseline import with its inlined fallback, block_angles, _ref_block_gates, masked_block_gates, _assert_topology / TOPOLOGY_OK, pauli_to_dense, build_h_tot, build_target, _sl, apply_h, apply_rz, apply_rx, apply_cx, apply_pauli_z, apply_pauli_x, apply_gate, simulate, _make_psi0, _block_schedule, _forward, objective, objective_and_grad, _grad_check / GRAD_CHECK_MAXERR, fit, assert_gates_ok, _emit, H_PREFIX, LAYERS/N_CHAINS/BLOCK_QUBITS/ANGLE_SEED/N_SLOTS/N_QUBITS/DIM/N_PARAMS, and the ANCHOR dict (values 0.8955/0.9164/0.9011/0.9228/0.9229 for INST-A..E). All changes are inside prepare(), plus new module-level constants and three new helpers.

B1. CONSTANTS. In the constants block (incumbent.py lines 80-81) DELETE both DEADLINE_S and MARGIN and every use of them, and add:
    SAFETY = 0.0005            # absorbs self-fit vs scorer disagreement (EXP-0013 measured ~2e-4)
    MAX_ROUNDS = 20            # fixed, deterministic; no wall-clock anywhere
    MAX_TRIAL_FITS = 520       # 35+34+...+16 = 510 trial fits fit inside this
    TRIAL_MAXITER = 400        # unchanged from the incumbent's tentative refit
    CONSOL_MAXITER = 1500      # unchanged
    CONSOL_INITS = 4           # unchanged
    FULL_MAXITER = 3000        # unchanged
    FULL_INITS = 8             # unchanged
    ESC_STAGES = 3             # escalated full-mask multistart stages
    ESC_INITS = 8
    ESC_MAXITER = 3000
Grep-clean requirement: after your edit, `grep -n 'DEADLINE\|MARGIN\|monotonic\|perf_counter\|time\.' workspace/candidate.py` must return NOTHING except, optionally, a single `diag['wall_s']` measurement that NO decision reads. The contract's dev-examples paragraph now requires a fixed iteration budget and forbids wall-clock deadlines; a deadline is the one thing that could make the five parallel instances non-exchangeable.

B2. NAME-KEYED SEEDS (contract requirement: 'key every RNG seed on payload["name"], NEVER on call order, a module-global counter, or wall-clock time'). Add, next to the constants:
    import hashlib
    def name_seed(name, offset):
        h = hashlib.sha256(('%s' % (name,)).encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()
        return (int(h[:12], 16) % 1000000) * 64 + int(offset)
Every fit() call in prepare() passes restart_seed = name_seed(name, k) with a FIXED literal k per call site: k=0 for the full-mask fit, k=1..ESC_STAGES for the escalation stages, k=2 + 100 (i.e. literal 102) + cost_after for the consolidation fit on a mask of size cost_after, and k=9 for the single-init trial fits (where n_restarts=1 makes the seed unused but the call must still be seeded consistently). No seed may depend on round_index, on a counter, or on which slot is being trialled beyond the cost_after term.

B3. NEW HELPER s_hat, placed immediately after fit():
    def s_hat(f_self, cost, anchor):
        """CONTRACT.md's per-instance score, computed on our own fidelity:
        s_i = 1000*max(0, F35_i - F_i) + C2_i, with SAFETY added to the anchor so a
        point we believe is exactly at the anchor is not scored as a win."""
        return 1000.0 * max(0.0, (anchor + SAFETY) - float(f_self)) + float(cost)
This is the ONLY objective used for any accept, reject or emit decision from here on. No other comparison of a fidelity to a threshold may exist in prepare().

B4. NEW HELPER record, placed after s_hat():
    def record(trace, tag, x, mask, f_self, anchor):
        cost = int(mask.sum())
        s = s_hat(f_self, cost, anchor)
        trace.append({'tag': str(tag), 'cost': cost, 'F_self': float(f_self), 's_hat': float(s)})
        return s, {'x': np.array(x, dtype=float), 'mask': mask.copy(),
                   'F_self': float(f_self), 'cost': cost, 's_hat': float(s), 'tag': str(tag)}
prepare() keeps diag['s_trace'] = [] and a variable best_point holding the dict with the smallest s_hat seen so far, updated ONLY on strictly-less-than so the earliest of equal points wins. Every point the run evaluates (full fit, each escalation stage, each trial refit, each consolidation refit) is passed through record().

B5. FULL-MASK FIT AND ESCALATION LADDER. This replaces incumbent lines 466-485 (the `thresh = anchor + MARGIN` line, the full fit, and the ENTIRE `if f_full < anchor - 0.001: ... return _emit(...)` abort). Delete the abort: it is the defect this cycle exists to remove. New logic:
    mask = np.ones(N_SLOTS, dtype=bool)
    x_full, f_full, recs_full = fit(block_angles(), mask, FULL_MAXITER, FULL_INITS, name_seed(name, 0), target)
    diag['full_structure'] = recs_full; diag['F_full'] = float(f_full)
    s_cur, pt = record(diag['s_trace'], 'full', x_full, mask, f_full, anchor)
    best_point = pt
    diag['full_below_anchor'] = bool(f_full < anchor)
    diag['escalation'] = []
    if f_full < anchor:
        for stage in range(1, ESC_STAGES + 1):
            x_e, f_e, recs_e = fit(x_full, mask, ESC_MAXITER, ESC_INITS, name_seed(name, stage), target)
            diag['escalation'].append({'stage': stage, 'F': float(f_e), 'records': recs_e})
            s_e, pt_e = record(diag['s_trace'], 'esc%d' % stage, x_e, mask, f_e, anchor)
            if s_e < best_point['s_hat']:
                best_point = pt_e
            if f_e > f_full:
                x_full, f_full = x_e, f_e
            if f_full >= anchor + SAFETY:
                break
Note fit()'s first init is always theta0, so passing x_full warm-starts from the best known angles and the remaining ESC_INITS-1 are fresh uniform(-pi, pi) draws from default_rng(seed). The ladder is a FIXED number of stages (no clock), it stops early only on clearing the anchor, and it NEVER aborts the cycle: whatever f_full ends up being, the descent in B6 runs.

B6. GREEDY DESCENT, s_hat-DRIVEN. This replaces incumbent lines 487-544. Keep the incumbent's structure (one round per removal; one TRIAL_MAXITER single-init trial refit per live slot; then one CONSOL_MAXITER x CONSOL_INITS consolidation refit on the accepted removal) with exactly these differences:
  (a) BUDGET: maintain an integer fits_used, incremented once per trial fit. The round loop condition becomes `while int(mask.sum()) > 0 and round_index < MAX_ROUNDS and diag['stop_reason'] is None`, and inside the slot loop, before each trial fit, `if fits_used >= MAX_TRIAL_FITS: diag['stop_reason'] = 'fit_budget'; break`. Record diag['fits_used'] and diag['rounds'] at the end. There is NO time check anywhere.
  (b) SELECTION: the accepted slot is the one MINIMIZING s_hat(f_trial, cost-1, anchor) over the live slots, not the one maximizing f_trial. Pass every trial point through record() with tag 'trial:r%d:s%d' % (round_index, s) and update best_point from it.
  (c) ACCEPTANCE: let s_cur = s_hat(f_cur, int(mask.sum()), anchor) and s_best the minimum over this round's trials. Accept iff s_best < s_cur - 1e-9. If not, set diag['stop_reason'] = 'no_s_hat_improving_removal' and break. There is NO absolute fidelity threshold in this test: a debt instance is allowed to prune, which is the entire point of the cycle.
  (d) CONSOLIDATION: after the consolidation fit produces (x_c, f_c) at cost_after = int(new_mask.sum()), record it with tag 'consol:%d' % cost_after and update best_point. If s_hat(f_c, cost_after, anchor) >= s_cur, set diag['stop_reason'] = 'consolidation_regression' and break WITHOUT discarding anything: the trace already holds every point and B7 emits the arg-min, so a regression costs the round, never the run.
  (e) Then set mask, theta, f_cur to the consolidated point and continue even if its s_hat is worse than best_point's: the descent may pass through a bump and the arg-min protects the result.
  (f) DELETE the incumbent's `if not round_complete or not trials: break` discard of a partially-completed round (incumbent lines 518-520). A budget-truncated round's trial points are legitimate evaluated points and are already in the trace; on a 'fit_budget' stop, break out of both loops and fall through to emission.
  (g) Keep diag['trace'] (the [cost, F] pairs) and diag['round1_table'] exactly as the incumbent builds them: the writer needs the fidelity-vs-cost curve. Keep diag['removed_slots'].

B7. EMISSION. Replaces incumbent lines 546-552. Emit best_point, not the loop's final state:
    p = best_point
    gates = H_PREFIX + masked_block_gates(p['x'].reshape(LAYERS, BLOCK_QUBITS, 2), p['mask'])
    f_sim = float(abs(np.vdot(target, simulate(gates))) ** 2)
    if abs(f_sim - p['F_self']) > 1e-9:
        raise RuntimeError('forward/simulate disagreement %r' % (f_sim - p['F_self'],))
    diag['emitted'] = {'tag': p['tag'], 'cost': p['cost'], 'F_self_fit': p['F_self'],
                       'F_self_sim': f_sim, 's_hat': p['s_hat'], 'anchor': float(anchor)}
    diag['final_cost'] = int(p['cost']); diag['final_F_self'] = f_sim
    diag['s_hat_emitted'] = float(s_hat(f_sim, p['cost'], anchor))
    diag['n_trace_points'] = len(diag['s_trace'])
    return _emit(gates, diag)
The raise is the one hard failure allowed, and B8's guard catches it, so it degrades rather than crashes. It exists because the emitted fidelity must come from the ACTUAL gate list, never from the optimizer's internal forward.

B8. GUARD. Keep the existing except-Exception block with one change: if best_point is not None, rebuild gates from best_point['x'] and best_point['mask'] and emit that; only if best_point is None fall back to the full 35-cx seed-0 circuit (H_PREFIX + masked_block_gates(block_angles(), ones)). Keep diag['guard'] and diag['guard_traceback'] and the existing assert_gates_ok path via _emit. A guard fire must still return a valid circuit.

B9. OPTIONAL PARALLELISM. You MAY, but are not required to, parallelize the per-slot trial fits inside one round using multiprocessing with the fork context and at most 2 worker processes, as the contract's PERFORMANCE & DETERMINISM paragraph now permits. If you do: the mapping must be over a fixed, sorted list of live slots, results must be reassembled in slot order before selection, and no seed or decision may depend on completion order. If any part of that is not trivially satisfiable, do it serially. Correctness and determinism outrank speed here.

WHAT NOT TO DO. Do not read, open, glob or reference anything under scorekeeper_private/. Do not use payload keys other than the ones the incumbent already uses ('name', 'beta', 'h_cost', 'reference_state'). Do not add a second circuit family (no ma-QAOA layers this cycle). Do not widen the gate vocabulary beyond h/rz/rx/cx. Do not change the ANCHOR numbers: they are transcribed from CONTRACT.md's public Metric paragraph and are the only legal source of anchor fidelities. Do not reintroduce any absolute fidelity threshold into the accept path. Do not reintroduce a wall-clock deadline. Keep the import-time _assert_topology and _grad_check gates running; if you touch _grad_check at all, raise its step h rather than loosening its tolerance (AUDIT.md flagged h=1e-6 against a 1e-6 tolerance as thin headroom).
done_definition: workspace/candidate.py imports cleanly with both _assert_topology and _grad_check passing at import; defines prepare(payload) -> {'n_qubits': 8, 'gates': [...]}; and for each of the five instances returns a gate list using only h/rz/rx/cx on qubits 0..7 with cx count <= 35 and total gates <= 5000, with no exception escaping prepare(). Greps that must return NOTHING: 'MARGIN', 'DEADLINE', 'abort_full_structure_below_anchor', 'monotonic', 'perf_counter'. Every accept, reject and emit decision goes through s_hat(). Every fit() restart_seed is name_seed(payload['name'], <fixed literal>). The emitted circuit is the arg-min of s_hat over diag['s_trace'], and diag['emitted']['F_self_sim'] agrees with the fitted value to 1e-9. DIAG prints, per instance: name, anchor, F_full, full_below_anchor, escalation records, the full s_trace of (tag, cost, F_self, s_hat), trace, round1_table, removed_slots, fits_used, rounds, stop_reason, emitted {tag, cost, F_self_fit, F_self_sim, s_hat}, s_hat_emitted, n_trace_points, n_gates, c2_count.
reopen_condition: If this dies by the kill threshold, the selection-rule and optimizer-budget direction on the hardware-efficient block closes and reopens ONLY on this specific new fact: a measured DIAG record showing a full-mask (35-cx) fit that reaches F_full >= anchor + 0.0005 on the deficit instance within a total restart budget of <= 32 L-BFGS-B inits x 3000 iterations, i.e. proof that the missing basin is findable at a price one scored run can pay. Absent that measurement, the 0.022 debt is a property of the layered rz/rx-plus-linear-chain family's expressivity at that instance rather than of the optimizer, and no further restart-budget or acceptance-rule refinement is funded. The next funded shot is then the term-pruned ma-QAOA family (about 5 surviving weight-4 strings at 6 CNOTs each plus the 1-CX |I> prep, to land under 35 two-qubit gates), which must be pitched as a macro structural bet, not slipped in as a refinement.
